skill.name: minimal-run-and-audit
skill.description: Runs a selected non-training reproduction command, captures execution evidence, and prepares standardized audit outputs for AI repository workflows.
skill.summary: Run one selected smoke, inference, or evaluation command and summarize the reproduction evidence.
skill.author: lllllllama

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are documentation or reporting false positives. The confirmed issue is free-form command execution through --command in scripts/run_command.py. This is expected for the skill, but requires explicit trust and user control.

remediation.issue: Free-form command execution in the target repository
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running --command, and document that only trusted, short, non-training commands should be executed.

remediation.issue: Broad command surface for reproduction runs
remediation.suggestion: Prefer README-listed smoke, inference, or evaluation commands, and reject long-running training commands before invoking subprocess.run.

content.value_statement: Reproduction work often loses evidence from short smoke tests and partial runs. This skill runs the selected non-training command and writes concise audit outputs.
actual_capabilities: Run a selected smoke, inference, evaluation, or sanity command with a timeout.
Capture stdout, stderr, exit status, timeout state, and launch errors.
Parse simple numeric metrics from command output.
Compare git status before and after a run to report touched paths.
Prepare standardized reproduction outputs, including summaries and patch notes.
limitations: It does not choose the research target or paper claim to reproduce.
It is not intended for training jobs, resume workflows, or long-running experiments.
It executes local commands and should be used only with trusted repositories.
It records execution evidence but cannot prove scientific validity by itself.

use_cases.title: Verify a README smoke test
use_cases.description: Run the documented quick check and capture whether it completed, failed, or timed out.

use_cases.title: Record benchmark reproduction evidence
use_cases.description: Capture command output, metrics, and changed files after a selected evaluation run.

use_cases.title: Audit a patched reproduction attempt
use_cases.description: Summarize the run result and separate patch notes from execution evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Run a smoke command
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check after setup is complete.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the selected README smoke command for this repository. Capture the command, result, logs, timeout status, and output files.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an inference command
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate verification of a documented inference path.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the documented inference command with a short timeout. Report success, partial status, blockers, metrics, and touched files.

prompt_templates.title: Normalize a failed run
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review when the command does not complete.
prompt_templates.prompt: Normalize the evidence from this failed reproduction command. Explain the blocker, preserve logs, and avoid unsupported conclusions.

prompt_templates.title: Compare execution and patches
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced audit after small repository changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the selected evaluation command after the patch. Separate command evidence from patch evidence and write concise reproduction outputs.

output_examples.input: A README smoke test is selected after dependencies are installed.
output_examples.output: A concise report states the command, completion status, captured logs, detected metrics, and changed files.

output_examples.input: A documented evaluation command exits with an error.
output_examples.output: A partial result explains the exit code, main blocker, useful log lines, and next verification step.

output_examples.input: A small patch was applied before a sanity run.
output_examples.output: The output separates run evidence from patch notes and lists touched paths for review.

best_practices: Use commands that the user selected or that the README clearly documents.
Set a short timeout and label blocked, partial, and successful runs clearly.
Keep summaries factual and separate measured results from inferences.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for training startup, resume, or long-running jobs.
Do not invent metrics or claim success when the command only partially ran.
Do not hide repository changes inside the execution summary.

faq.question: What does this skill run?
faq.answer: It runs one selected smoke, inference, evaluation, or sanity command for a repository.

faq.question: Does it choose the reproduction target?
faq.answer: No. The target and command should already be selected before this skill is used.

faq.question: Can it run training jobs?
faq.answer: No. It is designed for short non-training verification commands only.

faq.question: What evidence does it capture?
faq.answer: It captures logs, exit status, timeout state, simple metrics, and repository file changes.

faq.question: Does it modify repository files?
faq.answer: The selected command may modify files. The skill records changed, new, and deleted paths.

faq.question: Is command execution safe by default?
faq.answer: No. Use it only with trusted repositories and commands approved by the user.
